sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 WebGPURenderer + TSL; Rapier 0.19.3; Web Audio; Gamepad API; AI Hub Session Protocol v1 client 1.4.0
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel shading, dark ink silhouettes, pastel alien dioramas
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and keyframe tracks, plus procedural motion
sourceInformation.audio: Code-generated music at 10% default, synthesized effects and Animalese-style gibberish voices; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub 1–4 player shared-world co-op; standalone 1–2 local co-op
sourceInformation.testing: 20 simulation checks including complete solo and four-pilot campaigns; 17 Chromium browser checks with file://, virtual controller, touch and generated audio; 16 network unit checks; 54 AI Hub checks across four scenarios; 17 build/metadata checks. Real controller, iOS hardware and listening feedback: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: No source research; native model knowledge. Required AI Hub protocol and client read directly.

testingFeedback: Testing and visual/code review caught 16 actionable issues; all fixed and recorded in qa-log.json.
2 critical issues: a Rapier descriptor API mismatch and literal-string bundle corruption. Both fixed.
The complete automated solo and four-pilot campaigns validated every world, all twelve rescues, and the final victory; the real AI Hub harness validated four network scenarios.
Headless WebGPU screenshots were blank. Renderer-state checks and headed compatibility screenshots provided useful evidence instead.
engineFeedback: Three.js TSL made stepped cel shading and reusable procedural materials straightforward; AnimationMixer animated the creatures and engines.
Used a rigid-body instance method on a Rapier descriptor; installed type definitions gave the correct method. Literal HTML insertion also needed replacement callbacks to preserve dollar signs.
The alternating defense/rescue simulation, controller menu navigation and host-authoritative cooperative world.
Headless WebGPU image capture and multi-iframe SwiftShader device loss. Single-page WebGPU checks passed; some harness frames used the renderer’s WebGL2 fallback.
More reliable headless WebGPU screenshots and clearer backend/device-loss diagnostics.
promptFeedback: The source-inspired mechanics, single-file deliverable and explicit controller-first requirements provide a clear target.
The research ban alongside mandatory online integration was interpreted as no source research, with direct access to required protocol files.
Completing the campaign, input modes, procedural art and real multiplayer in one portable HTML file.
State explicitly that reading required integration files is allowed without source research.
